subject.title: Feature request: Shareable cron job templates

question: Should ClawHub support shareable scheduled-job templates as a first-class catalog/install surface, or should authors use existing skills/plugins until OpenClaw defines scheduled-job install semantics?
rationale: The request adds a new artifact and recurring-action trust boundary that current code and policy do not define, so automation should not choose the product or security model.

options.title: Design first-class cron templates
options.body: Define schema, preview, install authority, moderation, and OpenClaw runtime semantics before implementation.

options.title: Use existing skills or plugins
options.body: Keep cron examples as ordinary skill/plugin content and avoid a new artifact type for now.

options.title: Defer to runtime contract
options.body: Leave this open until OpenClaw defines installable scheduled-job semantics that ClawHub can publish safely.

recommendation.title: Design first-class cron templates
recommendation.body: Define schema, preview, install authority, moderation, and OpenClaw runtime semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the strongest current-history owner for the catalog schema, package docs, listing UI, and product-scope guardrails involved in this decision.
